title: A Risk Prediction System Based on Machine Learning for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation
journal: International Convention on Rehabilitation Engineering & Assistive Technology
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) significantly increases the risk of acute ischemic stroke (AIS), which may lead to disability and death. It is a clinical challenge for the risk assessment and management of AF. In this study, 5,330 cases were obtained from the Department of Cardiology, Chinese PLA General Hospital, containing demographic information, laboratory results, medical history, and other clinical variables. After preprocessing the data and using the random forest method to fill in the missing values, 12 variables with significant differences were selected as the features of the prediction model. To address the issue of imbalanced categories in the dataset, we implemented the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to achieve a balanced distribution of samples between the two categories. Five machine learning algorithms were used to establish prediction models. After comprehensive evaluation and comparison, the XGBoost algorithm, with an AUC of 0.908 (95% CI 0.872-0.938), demonstrated superior performance in AIS risk prediction among the five machine learning methods tested. The model was implemented within a user-friendly local prediction system constructed using the Flask framework. Predictions of AIS risk were provided to healthcare professionals, accompanied by a graphical representation illustrating the impact of individual patient characteristics on the predicted outcome. Our study shows the potential of machine learning techniques in enhancing stroke risk assessment among patients with AF, offering clinicians a valuable tool for early identification and intervention in high-risk individuals. With the system's predictions, doctors may be able to intervene earlier in the rehabilitation of patients, potentially speeding up the recovery process and mitigating the onset of stroke symptoms.

title: A Comparative Analysis for Stroke Risk Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Convolutional Neural Network Model
abstract: A critical, sometimes fatal medical disease called a stroke happens when the blood flow to a portion of the brain is broken off. In the case of stroke, urgent treatment is very essential. Nowadays, stroke is the main cause of death and impairment globally, according to WHO. In this situation, it will be very helpful if we predict the probability of stroke earlier depending on some most important features. Many researchers use different machine learning algorithms for prediction but very few researchers use stacking methods and CNN. The main contribution of this paper is to develop a stacking classifier of ensemble methods and the CNN model. In this paper, data-set is collected from Kaggle. Stroke data is imbalanced. Random oversampling is used for balancing data-set. Then most important features are find out using feature selection method, then applying different machine learning algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Decision Tree Classifier, Support vector machine, Random forest classifier, KNearest neighbour's classifier, Bernoulli Naïve Bayes, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, Stacking of six algorithms (Decision Tree Classifier, Support vector machine, Random forest classifier, KNearest neighbor's classifier, Bernoulli Naïve Bayes, Gaussian Naïve Bayes) and CNN. Then comparing the performances for predicting the probability of stroke during both the training and testing periods. Results show that the Stacking of six algorithms gives the highest accuracy, which is 99.89% for testing and 100% for training.

title: An Ensemble Machine Learning Approach for Imbalanced Brain Stroke Prediction
journal: 2026 6th International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Early detection of brain stroke can play an important role in reducing deaths and enhancing outcomes, but it is a challenging task owing to class imbalance in datasets, with the stroke-positive patients being minority samples (ratio of 19:1). This study evaluates and optimizes ensemble learning architectures by testing four machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and Neural Networks. The class imbalance issue is handled by employing hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV along with a unique algorithmic weighting technique that incorporates the use of both XGBoost and SVM in soft voting. Additionally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) technique determined the important predictor variables, which included age and clinical factors, like hypertension and mean blood glucose values. Overall, this study has shown that ensemble methods applying gradient boosting and SVM algorithms provide better prediction results in assessing clinical stroke risk, with a final optimal accuracy rate of 95.04%.

title: A Machine Learning Stacking Ensemble for Cerebral Stroke Prediction and Early Risk Assessment
journal: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
abstract: Cerebral stroke is a critical neurological disorder where early and proper risk forecasting is necessary to minimize death and permanent disability. Conventional diagnostic methods can be manual and time consuming which restricts their applicability in the timely intervention. In the present paper, a machine learning framework based on stacking ensembles is suggested to use in the prediction of cerebral strokes. The framework combines the use of CatBoost, Decision Tree, and Random Forest as base learners to utilize their relative predictive advantages. An end-to-end machine learning pipeline is built that involves the pre-processing of data, features encoding, and normalization, minimization of class imbalance with the help of the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), applied to the training data only to avoid data leakage. Eleven machine learning models were first tested on an imbalanced Kaggle stroke dataset and the best models were chosen in building an ensemble, in a performance comparative analysis. As it is experimentally proved, the proposed stacking ensemble is better than the individual classifiers and results in the overall prediction accuracy of 98.64 percent and the enhanced precision, recall, and F1-score. In order to achieve practical usefulness, the trained model is implemented in the form of a web-based application, which can make real-time predictions of the risk of stroke based on patient demographic and clinical characteristics. The suggested framework has a promising future as a dependable decision-support platform of smart healthcare systems and prompt stroke risk detection.

title: Automated Stroke Prediction using Machine Learning with a Web-Based Application for Early Risk Assessment
journal: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
abstract: Stroke is a life-threatening medical condition caused by disruption of blood flow to the brain, leading to neurological damage. Early prediction and intervention are vital to reduce the severe health and economic burdens posed by stroke globally. The existing automated stroke prediction systems utilize machine learning models trained on clinical datasets, achieving reasonable accuracy in identifying high-risk patients. However, these systems face limitations including imbalanced datasets, potential data leakage, a lack of comprehensive external validation, and limited interpretability of model decisions which can hinder clinician trust and adoption. Addressing these limitations, this study proposes an advanced stroke prediction system incorporating explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques such as SHAP and LIME that offer transparent and interpretable insights into the model’s decision-making process. The system integratesrobust feature selection, data balancing via SMOTE, avoidance of data leakage, and comparative evaluation of multiple classifiers including Random Forest and XG Boost, which achieve high accuracy and balanced precision-recall metrics. Furthermore, an end-to-end web and cross-platform mobile application is developed to facilitate real-time use by patients and healthcare providers, enhancing accessibility and usability for early stroke risk detection and timely intervention. KEYWORDS: neurological damage, potential data leakage, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), SHAP and LIME,Random Forest and XG Boost, interpretability

metadata_raw.tldr: An advanced stroke prediction system incorporating explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques such as SHAP and LIME that offer transparent and interpretable insights into the model’s decision-making process is proposed that achieves high accuracy and balanced precision-recall metrics.

title: Enhancing Brain Stroke Risk Prediction with Multi-Algorithm Evaluation and Web Interface
journal: 2024 International Conference on Engineering & Computing Technologies (ICECT)
abstract: Brain stroke is the world's leading cause of death, impacting numerous lives annually. The chances of having a stroke have increased by 50% over one's lifetime, impacting one in four people worldwide. Machine learning may assist in the prior detection of strokes, allowing for more timely diagnosis which can save a person's life and disability. However, existing methods face challenges in integrating ML models with clinical applications to predict patient stroke status with optimal accuracy. This study conducts a comprehensive investigation into brain stroke risk prediction using numerous ML algorithms, including Random Forest, Logistic Regression, KNN, Naive Bayes, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Our main contribution is the development of a web app that predicts stroke based on user inputs with optimal accuracy. The selected dataset contains 5110 records of normal people and 249 records of people having strokes which is highly imbalanced. To ensure model robustness, the dataset undergoes balancing through SMOTE oversampling and KNN Imputation for handling missing values. Custom thresholds for classifiers optimize training, with comprehensive evaluations utilizing key statistics such as confusion matrices, F1-Score, recall, accuracy, and precision. Cross-validation is employed to assess potential overfitting and underfitting risks in machine learning models. Random Forest ranked as the most imposing, reaching a remarkable 99.85% accuracy on the test set with a custom threshold of 0.6 and a random state at 42. Additionally, a user-friendly Web App has been developed to predict stroke status based on user input, enhancing practical usability and accessibility for individuals seeking risk assessments.

title: Approaches for handling imbalanced data used in machine learning in the healthcare field: A case study on Chagas disease database prediction
abstract: Machine learning has increasingly gained prominence in the healthcare sector due to its ability to address various challenges. However, a significant issue remains unresolved in this field: the handling of imbalanced data. This process is crucial for ensuring the efficiency of algorithms that utilize classification techniques, which are commonly applied in risk management, monitoring, diagnosis, and prognosis of patient health. This study conducts a comparative analysis of techniques for handling imbalanced data and evaluates their effectiveness in combination with a set of classification algorithms, specifically focusing on stroke prediction. Additionally, a new approach based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Naive Bayes was proposed. This approach was applied to the real problem of Chagas disease. The application of these techniques aims to improve the quality of life for individuals, reduce healthcare costs, and allocate available resources more efficiently, making it a preventive action.

metadata_raw.tldr: A comparative analysis of techniques for handling imbalanced data is conducted and their effectiveness in combination with a set of classification algorithms, specifically focusing on stroke prediction is evaluated, specifically focusing on stroke prediction.

title: Imbalanced Data Handling for Stroke Prediction Using Oversampling and Cost-Sensitive Learning
journal: 2025 8th International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
abstract: Class imbalance is a major challenge in medical predictive modeling, especially in stroke risk identification, where minority cases represent only a small fraction of the available clinical data. This study compares the effectiveness of two imbalance handling techniques, SMOTE oversampling and cost-sensitive learning, applied to Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XGBoost using the public Kaggle stroke dataset. Three experimental scenarios were evaluated: baseline, SMOTE, and cost-sensitive learning. The results show a significant improvement in minority class recall, especially for SVM, although this improvement is accompanied by a decrease in overall precision and accuracy. Evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC shows that cost-sensitive learning provides the best balance between sensitivity and discrimination performance. Further SHAP analysis revealed that age and hypertension were the most influential predictors. Although these findings are promising, limitations related to dataset size and the risk of overfitting remain. Further research should explore hybrid imbalance handling methods and validation on larger and more diverse datasets to improve clinical applicability.

title: Design of a Novel Enhanced Machine Learning Model for Early Prediction of Cerebral Stroke Early Prediction of Brain Stroke
journal: International Journal of Computing and Digital Systems
abstract: : A stroke can happen when the blood supply to a certain region in the brain’s cortex is abruptly severed. Without adequate blood flow, brain cells will eventually die, and the extent of the damage will be inversely correlated with the area of the injured brain. Early symptom identification is essential for stroke prediction and encouraging healthy habits by giving helpful information. The solution to these issues is developing a precise and e ff ective early-stage prediction model employing analytical support in clinical decision-making with digitized patient information. Most research focuses on forecasting cardiovascular stroke, but the cerebral risk for stroke has gotten far less attention. The current study aims to progress and assess several machine learning models to create a framework for predicting the long-term potential of cerebral stroke. By conducting a thorough experimental assessment using two di ff erent methodologies, namely SMOTE and SMOTE ENN, the suggested work tried to address the issue of imbalanced data from the Kaggle dataset. On SMOTE-Balanced as well as SMOTE ENN-balanced datasets, several models such as K-nearest neighbour (KNN), logistic regression(LR), support vector machine(SVM), decision tree(DT), random forests, XG boosting, stacking, and ANN are trained. As demonstrated by the results, SMOTE ENN and the stacking classification approach achieved a remarkable 99.52% accuracy, with a recall of 99.30%, a precision of 99.4%, and an F1 measure of 99%. We found that a relatively simple data balancing technique combined with a supervised machine learning algorithm can be used to predict strokes with high accuracy and great practical potential.

metadata_raw.tldr: It is found that a relatively simple data balancing technique combined with a supervised machine learning algorithm can be used to predict strokes with high accuracy and great practical potential.

title: Prediction of the Occurrence of Stroke Based on Machine Learning Models
journal: Computer Design Systems Theory and Practice
abstract:
The research conducted in the medical domain addressed a topic of significant
 importance, steadily growing in relevance each year. The study focused on predicting the
 onset of strokes, a condition posing a grave risk to individuals' health and lives.
 Utilizing a highly imbalanced dataset posed a challenge in developing machine learning
 models capable of effectively predicting stroke occurrences. Among the models examined,
 the Random Forest model demonstrated the most promising performance, achieving
 precision, recall, and F1-score metrics of 90%. These findings hold potential utility
 for healthcare professionals involved in stroke diagnosis and treatment.

metadata_raw.tldr: Among the models examined, the Random Forest model demonstrated the most promising performance, achieving precision, recall, and F1-score metrics of 90%.

title: Prediction of Stroke Hematoma Expansion Using a Machine Learning Model with Stacked Generalization
abstract: Hemorrhagic stroke is a prevalent global disease. Following hemorrhagic stroke, hematoma expansion emerges as a crucial prognostic risk factor. Currently, most prediction models for hematoma expansion rely on traditional machine learning algorithms [1]. However, these standalone machine learning algorithms often struggle to meet the desired accuracy levels for prediction. Additionally, public sample data frequently exhibit imbalanced characteristics, posing challenges during model training. To address this issue of imbalanced sample data, this study employs Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to oversample the minority samples within the dataset and generate more representative instances [2]. Subsequently, multiple models including Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) are trained and evaluated accordingly. Based on comprehensive evaluation results, we propose a stacked generalization-based model fusion approach that combines and stacks the aforementioned five models together. The findings demonstrate that the fused model after stacked generalization exhibits superior predictive performance by accurately forecasting hematoma expansion among patients—a significant contribution towards enhancing patient prognosis.

title: Optimizing Cerebral Stroke Prediction: Combining SMOTE-ENN and XGBoost on Imbalanced Medical Data
abstract: Cerebral stroke remains a major global health burden, ranking among the leading causes of death and longterm disability. Rapid and accurate identification of high-risk individuals is crucial for effective intervention and improved outcomes. However, clinical stroke prediction is often hindered by extreme class imbalance, where confirmed stroke cases are vastly outnumbered by non-stroke instances, resulting in high false negative rates with traditional machine learning models. To overcome this limitation, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique with Edited Nearest Neighbors (SMOTE-ENN) for data balancing and noise reduction, followed by classification using eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Evaluated on a real-world dataset of 43,400 patient records, including 783 confirmed stroke cases, the model achieved 98.14% accuracy and 87.39% sensitivity, while reducing false negatives by 34% compared to the baseline approaches. This approach offers a promising direction for improving clinical decision support systems through earlier and more reliable prediction of stroke risk.

title: Optimizing Stroke Prediction in Machine Learning by Addressing Data Imbalance
journal: 2023 3rd International Signal Processing, Communications and Engineering Management Conference (ISPCEM)
abstract: Brain strokes, responsible for about 11% of global deaths annually according to the World Health Organization, pose significant health challenges. Machine learning aids in early stroke risk prediction and personalized assessment, optimizing medical resource allocation. However, the low frequency of stroke cases in datasets poses challenges for accurate stroke prediction by these models. Addressing this data imbalance is key for effective prediction. This article focuses on: (i) analyzing machine learning outcomes on imbalanced stroke dataset; (ii) comparing methods to address data imbalances; and (iii) using Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) techniques to achieve high accuracy while realistically identifying stroke incidents. The results demonstrate that the application of Random Under Sampling (RUS) was instrumental in identifying the top-performing model, which showed superior performance in stroke prediction.

title: Brain Stroke Disease Prediction Using Cost-Sensitive Learning for Imbalanced Clinical Data
journal: 2026 International Conference on Innovations in Emerging Technologies for Sustainable Development (ICIETSD)
abstract: Precise estimation of brain stroke based on clinical data is a critical issue in preventive healthcare and especially since the medical data on the incidence of stroke cases is highly skewed with the incidence being several times lower compared to that of non-stroke cases. Traditional models of machine learning, which are trained on this type of data, frequently favor general performance and do not do a sufficient job of identifying potential high-risk stroke patients in a manner that causes clinically unacceptable false-negative rates. As an effort of overcoming this, the paper shows a cost-sensitive learning-based brain stroke disease prediction framework based on structured clinical data. The proposed method attempts to introduce the costs of misclassification directly to the process of learning data rather than altering the distribution of the data, thus allowing the classifiers to impose greater costs to false cases of stroke prediction. Different cost-sensitive ensemble learning models are tested to determine their ability to deal with class imbalance on the algorithm level. The results indicate that the concept of machine learning models implementing cost awareness is a promising and clinically relevant solution to predict the risk of a stroke, and the method is viable to be applied to the real-world decision-support system.

title: Optimizing decision thresholds and model selection for imbalanced clinical risk prediction: an ensemble framework for single-disease screening
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Machine Learning and Image Processing
abstract: Chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease, stroke, and cirrhosis impose substantial clinical and economic burdens, yet predictive models often falter in the presence of severe class imbalance and suboptimal decision thresholds. This study proposes an imbalance-ratio–aware, threshold-optimized ensemble for single-disease risk prediction. The framework adapts its learning route to the observed imbalance ratio, integrates synthetic oversampling and cost-sensitive learners when imbalance is pronounced, and fuses calibrated probabilities from the top performers using validation F1-based weights. Decision thresholds are tuned on precision–recall characteristics rather than fixed at 0.5, separating probability estimation from policy and aligning operating points with clinical priorities. For stroke (extreme skew), the ensemble increased recall to 0.6000 and improved F1 to 0.3659, raising G-Mean and MCC to 0.7404 and 0.3519, with an optimized threshold of 0.6880. For heart disease, the model sustained F1 at 0.9065 and lifted ROC-AUC to 0.9328 at a threshold of 0.4339. For cirrhosis, F1 reached 0.8571 with recall 0.8438 and threshold 0.3439. Averaged across tasks, F1, ROC-AUC, G-Mean, and MCC were 0.7098, 0.8956, 0.8348, and 0.6353, respectively. These findings indicate that coupling imbalance-aware training with threshold optimization yields robust, clinically meaningful performance. Future work will extend external validation, utility-constrained thresholding, and domain adaptation to strengthen deployment in real-world screening pipelines.

metadata_raw.tldr: Findings indicate that coupling imbalance-aware training with threshold optimization yields robust, clinically meaningful performance in single-disease risk prediction.

title: Predicting the Risks of Brain Stroke Using Machine Learning Models and Artificial Neural Network
abstract: The primary cause of death and disability worldwide is stroke. Accurate prediction models and identification of stroke risk factors can aid in early intervention and preventive measures. In this study, an approach based on machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), AdaBoost (AdB), Gradient Boosting (GB), Decision Tree (DT), and a unique Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model, is proposed to predict stroke risk at four different levels. To address the issue of imbalanced dataset, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique coupled with Edited Nearest Neighbors (SMOTEENN) was used. 11 features were selected for training the models out of the initial 12 features, and the data-set was divided into an 80–20 train-test ratio for model assessment. The Decision Tree (DT) model achieved an accuracy of 98.53%. Additionally, a 1000 epoch Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model with various batch sizes was created; 128 produced the best results. Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Adam, and RMSprop were examined along with other optimizers, however SGD produced the highest accuracy rate of 99.21%. The results suggest that utilizing the selected features and the balanced data-set, machine learning algorithms such as the unique CNN model can accurately predict stroke risk at various levels. These models have the potential to aid in early detection of stroke risk and guide preventive interventions, thus improving patient care and outcomes. Further testing and implementation of these models in real clinical settings are warranted.

title: Learning from Imbalanced Stroke Data: A Comparative Study of SMOTE and SMOTE-ENN on Structured Health Records
journal: International Conferences on Information Science and System
abstract: Stroke prediction with machine learning is challenged by severe class imbalance, which can produce models that appear accurate but fail to detect true stroke cases. This study evaluates Logistic Regression, SVM, and XGBoost on the Kaggle Stroke Prediction Dataset under three training regimes: no resampling, SMOTE, and SMOTE-ENN. Performance is assessed using imbalance-aware metrics (precision, recall, F1, and PR-AUC). Results show that models trained on the original data achieve high accuracy, yet near-zero recall for the stroke class, while SMOTE substantially improves minority-class detection and overall clinical usefulness. SMOTE-ENN offers additional sensitivity gains in some settings but introduces trade-offs in precision. These findings highlight the importance of resampling and appropriate evaluation metrics when developing stroke risk prediction models on imbalanced health records. Repeated cross-validation, SHAP-based explainability, and calibration analysis further indicate the models are best used as exploratory screening aids rather than deployment-ready clinical tools. These findings are expected to contribute to predictive maintenance in health monitoring for better future health and life.

title: Performance Analysis and Comparison of Cerebral Stroke Prediction Models on Imbalanced Datasets
journal: International Conference on Big Data, Cloud Computing, Data Science & Engineering
abstract: A cerebral stroke is an interrupt blood flow to the brain leading cause of death. A number of risk factors increase the risk of stroke occurence because of lifestyle. Machine learning is effective techniques can be applied in prediction of stroke. The different kind of algorithms give the various accuracy and performance in the prediction. This study has proposed the four machine learning algorithm for classifiers to predict of cerebral stroke. The proposed model with various classifier has considered the risk factors such as age, hypertension, heart disease, average glucose level, BMI, and smoking status as feature attributes to predict cerebral stroke. This study conducted on two stroke datasets, and improve the imbalanced of between classes by using SMOTE. The result shows that XGBoost provided the highest accuracy of around 98.08% and 96.73% by comparing to the other machine learning algorithms. In addition, this study evaluates the models by analyzing the statistical parameters include accuracy, precision, sensitivity, F1 score, and AUC. The evaluation reveals that the XGBoost, Random Forest, AdaBoost and KNN classifier achieved the average AUC value of 0.851, 0.868, 0.670 and 0.851, respectively. All models provided the high confidence values, whereas the model with XGBoost classifier gave the highest performance.

title: Integrated Classification Method with Hybrid Sampling for Stroke Prediction
abstract: This paper presents a novel supervised machine learning model, crafted to forecast the risk of stroke by analyzing a spectrum of contributing factors. Serving as an adjunct to medical professionals in their diagnostic endeavors, the model's predictive capabilities are pivotal, with the potential to avert fatalities and guide the adoption of preemptive strategies. The model underwent rigorous training and validation on an imbalanced dataset, which encapsulates a multitude of features linked to stroke risk. To optimize the model's performance, we employed hybrid sampling techniques to address the dataset's imbalance and utilized Grid Search to meticulously identify the most optimal parameters for our quintet of foundational models. Among these, the Integrated Classification Method distinguished itself by delivering exceptional precision, accuracy, F1-score, and recall within the range of 94.5%-95.5%. This level of performance underscores the model's robustness and its readiness to contribute significantly to the clinical decision-making process in the realm of stroke risk prediction.

metadata_raw.tldr: A novel supervised machine learning model, crafted to forecast the risk of stroke by analyzing a spectrum of contributing factors, distinguished itself by delivering exceptional precision, accuracy, F1-score, and recall within the range of 94.5%-95.5%.

title: Stroke Prediction Using a Stacked Ensemble Classifier
journal: International Conference on Critical Infrastructure Protection
abstract: A stroke occurs when there is a disruption or decrease in blood flow to various brain regions. As a result, the brain cells in those areas die from a lack of oxygen and nutrients. A stroke is a medical emergency that requires immediate attention. Early detection and effective therapy are necessary to prevent additional harm to the damaged area of the brain and its potential consequences in other sections of the body. This study presents a novel stroke risk prediction model utilizing a stacked ensemble approach that integrates multiple machine learning classifiers, including Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Addressing the challenges of imbalanced datasets, we employ a cost-sensitive learning technique and introduce logistic regression as a meta-learner to aggregate predictions from the base models, enhancing overall accuracy. Evaluating the proposed model across ten distinct medical datasets, our results demonstrate exceptional performance in terms of accuracy, recall, F1 score, precision, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), and Kappa, significantly outperforming all the traditional classifiers. This research underscores the potential of ensemble methods in improving stroke prediction accuracy and highlights the importance of leveraging diverse algorithms to achieve robust predictive capabilities. Our finding contributes to the ongoing efforts in healthcare analytics, paving the way for more effective stroke risk assessment and timely intervention strategies.

metadata_raw.tldr: This study presents a novel stroke risk prediction model utilizing a stacked ensemble approach that integrates multiple machine learning classifiers, including Adaptive Boosting, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Multilayer Perceptron, significantly outperforming all the traditional classifiers.

title: Application of Bayes Rule for Precise Analysis of Class-Imbalanced Stroke Data
journal: International Conference on Signals and Electronic Systems
abstract: The interpretability of stroke risk prediction is still lagging and it can be solved by using deep analysisofdata with the application of the Bayes rule. The prediction model has to be produced with accuracy, clarity, and comprehensibility without ambiguity, especially in machine learning and data analytics. The class imbalance problem is a common issue affecting the raw data, which means the imbalanced categorization of outcome feature value. In many fields, such as fraud detection, network intrusion detection, and medical diagnostics, this class imbalance issue is present where negative class samples outnumber positive class samples. If some datasets have class imbalance and imperfect issues, there will be no proper classification pattern. There are many resampling methods to address this class imbalance problem. However, these resampling methods can make an even distribution of classes by generating or omitting some samples, but theycannot handle imperfect data. The probabilistic analysis can lead to the identification of issues that exist in the dataset and provide direction to medical experts on dealing with the condition to avoid panic.The strength of applying the Bayes rule will provide a meaningful interpretation of stroke data. This paper investigates the Baye rule's significance in stroke data analysis.

title: Data-Driven Stroke Prediction: Leveraging KNN for Early Detection in Clinical Datasets
abstract: This study explores the application of the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm in predicting stroke risk using a healthcare dataset from Kaggle containing 5,110 patient records with demographic and clinical attributes. Preprocessing steps included categorical encoding, normalization, and feature engineering, followed by model training using a pipeline that incorporated SMOTE to address class imbalance. Hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV improved model performance. The final KNN model achieved an accuracy of 84%, with a recall of 0.64 and precision of 0.18 for the stroke class, indicating moderate sensitivity but significant false positive rates typical of imbalanced medical datasets. Evaluation metrics included the confusion matrix, ROC curve (AUC = 0.82), and precision-recall curve (AP = 0.19). While the model demonstrates reasonable discriminative ability, the low precision suggests limited utility as a standalone diagnostic tool. These findings contribute to the growing body of research on machine learning for clinical decision support, emphasizing the need for balanced performance metrics in imbalanced datasets and highlighting KNN's potential as a preliminary screening instrument when combined with clinical judgment.

metadata_raw.tldr: While the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm demonstrates reasonable discriminative ability, the low precision suggests limited utility as a standalone diagnostic tool, and highlighting KNN's potential as a preliminary screening instrument when combined with clinical judgment.

title: Stroke Prediction with Explainable AI and PR-AUC–Driven Model Selection
journal: 2026 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
abstract: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability, and early risk identification can support timely clinical screening. In practice, stroke datasets are highly imbalanced, which can make accuracy appear high even when a model has limited usefulness for the minority (stroke) class. In this study, we evaluate multiple machine learning (ML) models for tabular stroke prediction under a unified preprocessing pipeline and perform model selection driven primarily by PR-AUC, which is more informative than accuracy in imbalanced settings. We compare Logistic Regression, SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting variants, Naïve Bayes, and a multilayer perceptron using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. We also analyze overfitting and underfitting trends using learning curves. Finally, we introduce explainable AI (XAI) to support transparency, combining global explanations with SHAP-based global and local explanations. Key novelties include the unified pipeline design, PR-AUC–driven model selection, and integrated global+local SHAP explanations. Quantitatively, the selected Logistic Regression achieved PR-AUC = 0.254±0.046 and ROC-AUC = 0.880±0.018 (5-fold CV), with Acc@0.5 = 0.786 and Recall@0.5 = 0.820 (Table I). The results indicate that a PR-AUC-optimized Logistic Regression model offers a strong trade-off between discrimination and interpretability, while threshold selection enables operating points suitable for balanced decision-making and high-recall screening.

title: Prediction of Cardiovascular and Renal Complications of Diabetes by a multi-Polygenic Risk Score in Different Ethnic Groups
abstract: We developed a multi-Polygenic risk score (multiPRS) to predict the risk of nephropathy, stroke, and myocardial infarction in people with type 2 diabetes of European descent. The underrepresentation of non-European populations remains a major challenge in genomics research. Objective: To evaluate the ability of our multiPRS model to accurately predict these complications in patients of African and South Asian descents. Method: The multiPRS was developed using 4098 participants with type 2 diabetes of European origin from the ADVANCE trial. Its predictive performance was tested on 17,574 White British, 1,145 South Asian and 749 African participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank using different machine learning prediction models, including techniques tailored for imbalanced datasets. Results: Globally, linear discriminant analysis and logistic regression had the best performance to predict the risk of nephropathy, stroke, and myocardial infarction in people with type 2 diabetes for the three ethnic groups. Mondrian Cross-Conformal Prediction method when added to logistic regression improved the AUROC values and case detection, particularly in South Asians and Africans, while in White British, performance varied by phenotype. Conclusion: Logistic regression, when used as the underlying model within the Modrian Cross-Conformal Prediction framework, improved the prediction performance, with a confidence level, of diabetes complications and allows better translation of a multiPRS derived from European populations to other ethnic groups.

metadata_raw.tldr: Logistic regression, when used as the underlying model within the Modrian Cross-Conformal Prediction framework, improved the prediction performance, with a confidence level, of diabetes complications and allows better translation of a multiPRS derived from European populations to other ethnic groups.

title: Predicting Cerebral Stroke: Comparison Between Anomaly Detection Algorithms and Classification Models
journal: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Cerebral stroke occurs due to hindered blood flow to various parts of the brain, often caused by ischemic blockages or haemorrhagic vascular rupture. These disruptions can lead to severe brain damage or death if not addressed promptly. Annually, over 15 million people worldwide suffer from cerebral stroke, with lifestyle factors such as hypertension and smoking playing a significant role. This study presents a comparative analysis of cerebral stroke prediction models utilizing classification algorithms—Random Forest, XGBoost, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, and KNN—as well as anomaly detection methods such as Local Outlier Factor, Isolation Forest, and Gaussian Probability Distribution. Among these, the Isolation Forest algorithm demonstrated superior performance, achieving a weighted TPR-TNR score of 0.7449, reflecting balanced anomaly detection capabilities in imbalanced datasets. The findings highlight the importance of tailored machine learning solutions for stroke risk prediction. Future work will explore hybrid approaches to enhance detection accuracy while addressing dataset challenges.

title: Enhancing Stroke Risk Prediction with Explainable AI: Leveraging Resampling and Machine Learning for Improved Accuracy
abstract:
Highlight:



Advanced resampling techniques improved class balance in stroke datasets

Gradient Boosting with SMOTE reached 92% accuracy with SHAP interpretability


ABSTRACT


Introduction: Stroke represents a significant global health concern, impacting millions worldwide and contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality. Early detection and accurate risk prediction remain critical for effective prevention strategies. Objective: This study aimed to improve stroke risk prediction by employing machine learning algorithms on health survey data to identify key predictors and enhance predictive performance. Method: A dataset derived from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, comprising 4,603 participants, was utilized. The dataset exhibited class imbalance, with only 7.86% of individuals diagnosed with stroke. To address this imbalance, advanced resampling techniques, including SMOTE, SMOTETomek, and ADASYN, were applied. A range of tree-based algorithms was implemented, including Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, XGBoost, and a Voting Classifier integrating Decision Tree, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting classifiers. Model evaluation included accuracy and AUC scores. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) analyses were conducted using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to interpret feature importance. Result: The Gradient Boosting classifier, in conjunction with SMOTE, achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 92% and an AUC score of 0.70. SHAP analysis identified age, general health condition, marital status, and BMI as the most influential predictors of stroke risk. Conclusion: This study underscores the essential need for ongoing advancements in early stroke detection methodologies. The findings highlight the transformative potential of machine learning and XAI in predictive healthcare, offering valuable insights for stroke prevention strategies.

metadata_raw.tldr: This study underscores the essential need for ongoing advancements in early stroke detection methodologies and highlights the transformative potential of machine learning and XAI in predictive healthcare, offering valuable insights for stroke prevention strategies.

title: Optimizing Stroke Risk Prediction: A Machine Learning Pipeline Combining ROS-Balanced Ensembles and XAI
abstract: Stroke is a major cause of death and permanent impairment, making it a major worldwide health concern. For prompt intervention and successful preventative tactics, early risk assessment is essential. To address this challenge, we used ensemble modeling and explainable AI (XAI) techniques to create an interpretable machine learning framework for stroke risk prediction. A thorough evaluation of 10 different machine learning models using 5-fold cross-validation across several datasets was part of our all-inclusive strategy, which also included feature engineering and data pretreatment (using Random Over-Sampling (ROS) to solve class imbalance). Our optimized ensemble model (Random Forest + ExtraTrees + XGBoost) performed exceptionally well, obtaining a strong 99.09% accuracy on the Stroke Prediction Dataset (SPD). We improved the model's transparency and clinical applicability by identifying three important clinical variables using LIME-based interpretability analysis: age, hypertension, and glucose levels. Through early prediction, this study highlights how combining ensemble learning with explainable AI (XAI) can deliver highly accurate and interpretable stroke risk assessment. By enabling data-driven prevention and personalized clinical decisions, our framework has the potential to transform stroke prediction and cardiovascular risk management.

metadata_raw.tldr: This study highlights how combining ensemble learning with explainable AI (XAI) can deliver highly accurate and interpretable stroke risk assessment and has the potential to transform stroke prediction and cardiovascular risk management.

title: PrecisionStroke: Optimized Stroke Risk Prediction through Advanced Hyperparameter Tuning and Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Stroke prediction is a challenging problem in the healthcare domain, especially due to high class imbalance in datasets where data about stroke cases is a very small portion. In this study we develop a machine learning based framework for stroke prediction that tackles through powerful data preprocessing methods, such as Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for balancing the classes. (Situated within the entire framework of a comparative evaluation of the Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and TabNet machine learning classifiers as per unique designs. In conclusion, the Random Forest classifier proved to be the best performing model with an accuracy of 99.38%, followed closely by LightGBM and CatBoost. A detailed analysis including KP song metrics including precision, F1 score, and confusion matrices were carried out to ensure thorough evaluation. The study also emphasizes the importance of explainable AI tools which improve the explainability of predictions. This framework shows that machine learning has the potential to assist with early detection of stroke and may ultimately be integrated into clinical decision-making systems.

title: Analysing an imbalanced stroke prediction dataset using machine learning techniques
journal: Karbala International Journal of Modern Science
abstract: A stroke is a medical condition characterized by the rupture of blood vessels within the brain which can lead to brain damage. Various symptoms may be exhibited when the brain's supply of blood and essential nutrients is disrupted. To forecast the possibility of brain stroke occurring at an early stage using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) is the main objective of this study. Timely detection of the various warning signs of a stroke can significantly reduce its severity. This paper performed a comprehensive analysis of features to enhance stroke prediction effectiveness. A reliable dataset for stroke prediction is taken from the Kaggle website to gauge the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The dataset has a class imbalance problem which means the total number of negative samples is higher than the total number of positive samples. The results are reported based on a balanced dataset created using oversampling techniques. The proposed work used Smote and Adasyn to handle imbalanced problem for better evaluation metrics. Additionally, the hybrid Neural Network and Random Forest (NN-RF) utilizing the balanced dataset by Adasyn oversampling achieves the highest F1-score of 75% compared to the original unbalanced dataset and other benchmarking algorithms. The proposed algorithm with balanced data utilizing hybrid NN-RF achieves an accuracy of 84%. Advanced ML techniques coupled with thorough data analysis enhance stroke prediction. This study underscores the significance of data-driven methodologies, resulting in improved accuracy and comprehension of stroke risk factors. Applying these methodologies to medical fields can enhance patient care and public health outcomes. By integrating our discoveries, we can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the public health system.

metadata_raw.tldr: This paper performed a comprehensive analysis of features to enhance stroke prediction effectiveness and underscores the significance of data-driven methodologies, resulting in improved accuracy and comprehension of stroke risk factors.

title: A Machine Learning and Explainable AI-Based Stroke Risk Prediction Approach With SHAP Based Advanced Interpretability
journal: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Stroke is a serious condition that needs to be diagnosed immediately with proper treatment and ML-based prediction. Previous literary works on stroke prediction mainly focus on binary prediction and ignore multiclass classification of stroke subtypes. The previous works experienced problems with class imbalance, poor feature selection, and decreased prediction accuracy. This work confers a ML based multiclass stroke classification framework that addresses these drawbacks by utilizing Bayesian Search-based hyper parameter tuning, SMOTE-NC-based class imbalance solving, feature selection through random forest, and sophisticated preprocessing. LightGBM is chosen as the best ML model for stroke prediction in this article due to its high F1 score (93.90%) and accuracy (93.94%). This paper also explains the interpretability of a global model based on SHAP. According to the comparative results, the proposed LightGBM model outperforms existing works by at least 3% higher accuracy value and F1 value.

title: From Imputation to Prediction: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Pipeline for Stroke Risk Analysis
journal: 2024 International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication and Applied Informatics (ACCAI)
abstract: This research sought to address the shortcomings of biostatistical methods in traditional practice brought about by a complex etiology structure associated with strokes using ML algorithms for stroke prediction. In clinical settings, problems such as obscure pipelines and the treatment of missing data are endemic. This study aims to develop a comprehensive ML pipeline that can compare the predictive power of various ML models and addresses class imbalance using SMOTE while incorporating advanced data imputation. The proposed methodology involves data preparation, use of PCA to reduce dimensions in order to compare the models including Logistic Regression, Random Forest LightGBM SVM and a deep learning framework. High accuracy (Random Forest: The results reveal that Random Forest and Deep Learning models are effective for stroke prediction as their precision, recall rates included $\sim 0.95$ (Random Forest: $\sim 0.94$), prove it Besides this, the LightGBM model demonstrated outstanding results with a good balance between specificity and sensitivity which is evident in high true-positive rates. Significant for stroke prediction, the research established that complex models elegantly deal with complicated data patterns. Future research will focus on the clinical practice integration of these models, having taken into account their computational efficiency and interpretability.

title: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Stroke Risk Prediction
journal: 2026 International Conference on AI Innovations and Industry (ICAIII)
abstract: This study introduces a robust machine learning framework that aims at enhancing stroke risk prediction and supporting global health objectives to reduce stroke-related morbidity and mortality. Utilizing the Kaggle Stroke Prediction Dataset, the research integrates advanced data preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, and the application of five machine learning algorithms: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM. A stacked ensemble model forms the methodological core, achieving superior predictive performance (accuracy 97%, F1-score 0.97, AUC-ROC 0.99) compared to individual models and prior works. Bayesian Optimization ensured optimal hyperparameter selection, while explainability methods such as SHAP and LIME bolstered model interpretability to meet clinical transparency demands. The methodology aligns with the NZ Ngā Tikanga Paihere Framework, embedding principles of data privacy, cultural sensitivity, and fairness. Addressing challenges like data imbalance and computational scalability via SMOTE and distributed computing, the model demonstrated robust performance validated through bootstrapping and crossvalidation. This research advances ethical, accurate, and actionable AI-driven stroke prediction for healthcare applications.

title: Brain Stroke Risk Prediction System Using Machine Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
abstract: Stroke is a major cause of death and long-term disability worldwide . Early prediction of the risk of stroke is important for preventive healthcare. This paper proposes a Machine Learning based Brain Stroke Risk Prediction System using a publicly available dataset of 4,981 patient records with 11 health-related features. The Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is used to solve the class imbalance. The framework includes data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, explainability analysis and deployment. We construct four more risk-related features to improve the prediction performance. Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost models are evaluated based on Accuracy, Recall, F1-Score and ROC-AUC metrics. Logistic Regression achieved the best ROC-AUC of 0.8467, while XGBoost was chosen for deployment due to its good performance and compatibility with explainable AI. SHAP is integrated for transparent feature-level explanations, and a Streamlit-based dashboard facilitates real-time stroke risk assessment and personalized healthcare recommendations. The proposed system offers a cheap, practical and interpretable decision support for early prediction of risk of stroke.

metadata_raw.tldr: A Machine Learning based Brain Stroke Risk Prediction System using a publicly available dataset of 4,981 patient records with 11 health-related features that offers a cheap, practical and interpretable decision support for early prediction of risk of stroke.

title: Stroke Risk Prediction Using Imbalance-Sensitive Machine Learning Models on Structured Clinical Data
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The high urgency of the issue of considering the early prediction of risks as an essential tool in the prevention of health and clinical decisions is preconditioned by the prevalence of stroke as one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability in the world. The presence of machine learning techniques in the field of automated stroke risk estimation is highly popular as accessibility to electronic health records rises. However, in practice, the numbers of healthcare are very often skewed extremely, and the incidences of stroke under consideration represent just a small part of the overall population. This bias is frequently followed by falsely high accuracy and failure to identify the cases of stroke, which reduces clinical utility. The study suggests a machine learning framework that is imbalanceaware in predicting stroke risk when structured clinical data are used. The suggested method incorporates preprocessing of data systematically, normalization of features, SMOTE, and cost-sensitive learning to improve the detection of the minority classes. Clinically relevant measures like precision, recall, and F1-score are used to determine model performance besides accuracy. The experimental findings indicate that imbalance control has a great effect on improving the ability to detect a stroke across all models. Logistic Regression had the best recall at 0.80 and F1-score at 0.2469, which means that it was the most effective in determining high-risk patients, even though it has a moderate accuracy. The code is available on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/aimlprojects2025/StrokeFiveMLAlgorithm

title: Attention-Guided Hybrid Machine Learning with Uncertainty Estimation for Personalized Stroke Risk Prediction
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract:
Stroke is among the top causes of incurable death and lifelong disability in the world, and the ability to predict the risk early is
essential to ensure timely intervention and prevention. This paper introduces a new hybrid machine learning model for
personalized stroke risk identification which combines an Attention-based TabNet framework, gradient boosting ensemble, and
Bayesian uncertainty estimation. The suggested system successfully processes patient demographic, clinical, and lifestyle data
with the help of a strict preprocessing pipeline, which corrects missing values, normalizes information, and reduces class
imbalance.
To increase the interpretability of the model and enhance patient individualization, an attention-guided feature selection
mechanism is used to identify the most significant risk factors. The gradient boosting ensemble model captures complex
nonlinear correlations among the features, whereas the Bayesian component measures predictive uncertainty, giving clinicians
confidence in high-risk predictions. The experimental findings show that the hybrid model is more effective than conventional
models such as XGBoost, Random Forest, and standalone TabNet, achieving higher accuracy, F1-score, and area under the
ROC curve.
Moreover, explainable AI methods offer practical knowledge about personal risk factors, aiding in individualized prevention
strategies. This framework provides a clinically useful tool for early stroke detection, making predictions interpretable and quantifying uncertainty to help health practitioners make decisions, decrease clinical burden, and enhance patient outcomes.

metadata_raw.tldr: This framework provides a clinically useful tool for early stroke detection, making predictions interpretable and quantifying uncertainty to help health practitioners make decisions, decrease clinical burden, and enhance patient outcomes.

title: Optimizing Stroke Risk Prediction Using SMOTEENN and Transfer Learning
journal: 2025 International Conference on Innovations and Emerging Technologies In AI & Communication Systems (IETACS)
abstract: Timely intervention through early risk prediction is critical as stroke occurs to be a leading cause of global death and disability. In this paper, a new method is developed that combines synthetic minority oversampling technique with edited nearest neighbors (SMOTEENN) and transfer learning for stroke risk prediction using the stroke prediction dataset from Kaggle. This dataset captures the target patient population's age, history of hypertension, and smoking, among other attributes. It combines SMOTEENN to manage class imbalance with a transfer learning architecture using a ResNet model remediated and retrained on tabular data to provide high performance in a federated learning framework. The results indicate a ROC AUC of 0.912 which is a associated with a balanced accuracy of 0.875, surpassing the performance of baseline machine learning models. The framework employs data federated learning which, in addition to its strong performance in healthcare, provides data privacy. This research showcases the accuracy hybrid methods can provide for timely, scalable stroke risk prediction.

title: An Intelligent Approach to Stroke Risk Forecasting Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Feature Engineering Techniques
journal: 2025 International Conference on Engineering & Computing Technologies (ICECT)
abstract: Stroke represents a significant global public health challenge due to its high association with death and disability; therefore, early identification and accurate risk stratification are essential for improving survival rates. However, conventional prediction models for stroke have repeatedly shown a lack of accuracy and reliability. The primary objective of this research is to introduce a refined computational architecture designed to enhance stroke risk stratification. Statistical cleansing in its preprocessing step was supplemented by incorporating use of Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for mitigating problems stemming from class imbalance. Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), as well as Forward Feature Selection (FFS), were used for feature selection. Hyperparameter tuning was conducted to optimize the performance of six distinct machine learning architectures: Logistic Regression, SVM, and Naïve Bayes, alongside K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, and Random Forest. The developed methodology first employs Genetic Algorithms to refine the feature space. Subsequently, this optimized data is processed by a hybrid model integrating K-Nearest Neighbors with Random Forest logic. Both hybrid framework and conventional approaches were found to result in an accuracy level of $94 \%$. Further analysis for feature relevance indicated age, average level of blood sugar, patient number for identity, BMI, and occupation as the leading predictors for incidence in stroke. These results show promise for hybrid machine learning approaches in enhancing prediction for risk in strokes and thus provide a foundation for more accurate clinical interventions.

title: Evaluating Stroke Risk with Single-Modality Learning: Machine Learning on Clinical Records vs. Deep Learning on Brain Scans
abstract: Stroke continues to be one of the top causes of death and long-term disability globally, explaining the necessity of early and precise prediction before intervention. This study presents a dual-modality system for the detection of stroke by combining the processing of structured clinical records with unstructured medical imaging data. Demographic and health parameters are contained in the clinical dataset, and CT and MRI brain scans are in the imaging. For structured data, 5 machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree) were applied to predict the risk of stroke. At the same time, imaging data were studied with the help of deep learning architectures such as a baseline CNN, AlexNet, and ResNet-50. For enhancing the quality of data, mean imputation was used to deal with missing values, while SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) was applied to class imbalance since only 5.2% of the clinical data were representing stroke cases. Results presented show the superiority of deep learning when compared to machine learning overall. The CNN model gave an accuracy of 97.20%, which surpassed both the highest-performing machine learning models (XGBoost and Random Forest), which scored 96.35%. The application of SMOTE and normalized preprocessing drastically enhanced the reliability and fairness of the model, particularly for minority class detection. According to this study, machine learning and deep learning are both capable of proficiently aiding stroke prediction, but they do so in different types of data. The future line of work will spur the development of a multimodal fusion model using the clinical and imaging data and will further vet the advanced CNN architectures and explainable AI (XAI) processes to improve the clinical interpretability and diagnostic confidence.

title: Cardiovascular disease risk prediction among people living with HIV in Uganda: A comparison of traditional statistical and machine learning models
journal: Journal of interventional epidemiology and public health
abstract:
Objective: To develop and compare the performance of traditional statistical models and machine learning (ML) algorithms for cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) risk prediction among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Uganda, and identify key predictors using interpretable AI tools.

Methods: Data from 1,000 adult PLHIV followed for 10 years at the Infectious Diseases Institute, Kampala were analyzed. CVD was defined as a composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease. Models included Logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards, and ML algorithms (Decision Tree, Random Forests, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, and Soft Voting Ensemble). Class imbalance was handled using the SMOTE, and hyperparameters were tuned through a grid search with 10-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall and F1-Score. Feature importance was examined with SHAP and permutation analyses. 

Results: Of the participants, 61.7% were female, median age was 55 years, median ART duration 231.7 months, and median CD4 count was 504 cell/µl. Most had a viral load of <400copies/Ml (91.3%), self-employed (58.3%) and married/cohabiting (50.8%). During follow-up 31.8% developed CVDs, more commonly among those ≥55years (34.7% vs 28.3%, P=0.03), with hypertension (36.3% vs 28.6, P=0.01) or diabetes (43.2% vs 30.4%, P=0.06). No differences seen by gender, employment or substance use. The median ART duration before CVDs onset was 232.3 months. Traditional models showed moderate predictive ability (AUC < 0.65), Soft Voting Ensemble achieved best performance (AUC: 0.812) and feature importance highlighted, CD4 count, hypertension, diabetes, alcohol usage, age, marital and employment status as key predictors.

Conclusion: Nearly one-third of the participants developed CVDs. ML ensemble models substantially outperformed Traditional models for CVD risk prediction, while interpretable ML identified clinically relevant predictors. These findings support integration ML tools into HIV care to strengthen CVD risk stratification and prevention.

metadata_raw.tldr: ML ensemble models substantially outperformed Traditional models for CVD risk prediction, while interpretable ML identified clinically relevant predictors, and support integration ML tools into HIV care to strengthen CVD risk stratification and prevention.

title: Characterisation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) incidence and machine learning risk prediction in middle-aged and elderly populations: data from the China health and retirement longitudinal study (CHARLS)
abstract: Due to the ageing population and evolving lifestyles occurring in China, middle-aged and elderly populations have become high-risk groups for cardiovascular disease (CVD). The aim of this study was to analyse the incidence characteristics of CVD in these populations and develop a prediction model by using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). We used follow-up data from the CHARLS to analyse CVD incidence in the Chinese middle-aged and elderly population over a time span of 9 years. Five machine learning (ML) algorithms were employed for risk prediction. Data preprocessing included missing value imputation via random forest. Feature selection was performed using the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (Lasso CV) method with cross-validation prior to model training. The application of the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated via analyses including the area under the ROC curve (AUC), precision, recall, F1 score, and SHAP plots for interpretability. In accordance with the exclusion criteria, 12,580, 12,061, 11,545, and 11,619 participants were enrolled in four follow-up rounds. The cumulative incidence (CI) of CVD at 2, 4, 7, and 9 years was 2.846%, 8.971%, 17.869% and 20.518%,, respectively. Significant differences in CVD incidence were observed across gender, age, ethnicity, and region, with higher rates observed in females and in the northeast region. Ultimately, 8,080 participants and 24 features were analysed for CVD risk prediction. Five ML models were built based on these features. Although the LGB model achieves an AUC of 0.818, indicating strong overall performance, its F1 score and recall rate are relatively low, at 0.509 and 43.1%, respectively. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses revealed the importance of key features, such as night sleep duration, TG levels, and waist circumference, in predicting outcomes, and highlighted the nonlinear relationships between these features and CVD risk. Gender, age, ethnicity, and region are significant factors influencing CVD incidence. Although the LGB model demonstrates good overall performance, its low F1 score and recall rate reveal limitations in identifying high-risk cardiovascular disease patients.

metadata_raw.tldr: Analysis of CVD incidence in the Chinese middle-aged and elderly population over a time span of 9 years revealed the importance of key features, such as night sleep duration, TG levels, and waist circumference, in predicting outcomes, and highlighted the nonlinear relationships between these features and CVD risk.

title: Machine Learning-based Predictive Model for Ischemic Stroke Risk Assessment: A Data-Driven Approach using XGBoost
journal: 2025 9th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide, requiring early and accurate prediction for timely intervention. This study proposes an XGBoost-based machine learning model for stroke prediction using structured patient data, including demographics, medical history, and hospital visit records. The dataset, consisting of 5,147 patient records, was preprocessed through missing value imputation, feature selection, normalization, and class balancing. To address class imbalance, random undersampling was applied, ensuring the model learned effectively from both stroke and non-stroke cases. The proposed model achieved 94.4% accuracy and 0.91 AUC-ROC, outperforming traditional models such as Random Forest and Logistic Regression. Feature importance analysis identified age, NIH Stroke Scale Score, hypertension, and cardiologist visits as key predictors. Comparative evaluation demonstrated that our model surpassed prior research in stroke classification. By integrating gradient boosting, feature engineering, and class balancing, this study provides a highly interpretable and clinically valuable model for ischemic stroke prediction, aiding healthcare professionals in early diagnosis and risk assessment.

title: Solving Imbalanced Data in Credit Risk Prediction: A Comparison of Resampling Strategies for Different Machine Learning Classification Algorithms, Taking Threshold Tuning into Account
abstract: Effective credit risk prediction is critical for commercial banks to actively manage their lending book and reduce negative impact from potential credit losses. In a benign credit markets where default rates are low, the datasets for customers’ credit default status prediction are often imbalanced. While many studies have been conducted to address the class imbalance problem in the machine learning field under various contexts, our research focuses on the credit risk sector. We experiment five resampling strategies (SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, Random Undersampling, NearMiss, SMOTE + Tomek Links) and a thresholding technique (Optimal G-Mean) on eight different classifiers separately. We also explore whether the combination of resampling and thresholding can enhance the overall classifier performance. The performance of models is evaluated on both threshold metrics (G-Mean, F1-score) and ranking metrics (area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve). Our findings suggest that pure threshold tuning can often outperforms resampling methods whereas the effect of thresholding on the basis of resampled dataset is minor.

metadata_raw.tldr: The findings suggest that pure threshold tuning can often outperforms resampling methods whereas the effect of thresholding on the basis of resampled dataset is minor.

title: Stroke Prediction on Healthcare Data Using SMOTE and Explainable Machine Learning
journal: International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security
abstract: The early detection and prevention of stroke stands as a vital healthcare priority because this condition leads to major disabilities and deaths worldwide. This study introduces an efficient machine learning system which predicts stroke risk through analysis of clinical and demographic information. The dataset contained an extreme class imbalance because strokes occurred in only 4.87 % of patients. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was used to balance the dataset until it reached a 50 % -50 % distribution. The research compared four machine learning algorithms through implementation: Lo-gistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and CatBoost. The CatBoost classifier produced the best results among all models with an accuracy rate of 95.58 % and precision rate of 96.82 % and recall rate of 94.23 % and Fl-score of 95.51 %. The study employed explainable machine learning approaches to reveal how the model made decisions which improved both interpretation and clinical decision support. The proposed model demonstrates better performance than baseline methods and shows potential to assist clinicians with stroke risk assessment.

title: Brain Stroke Prediction: A PSO Optimized Stacked Ensemble Machine Learning Approach with SMOTEEN Data Balancing
abstract: Prediction of stroke is a critical challenge in healthcare, where early intervention can significantly reduce risks and improve patient outcomes. Traditional methods often struggle with imbalanced datasets and low prediction accuracy. This paper proposes a novel approach to address these issues by combining PSO-optimized Stacked Ensemble ML Classifiers with SMOTEEN data balancing to predict strokes effectively. The technique optimizes 3 Baseline ML Classifiers(RF, SVM, XGB) using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Stacked Ensemble approach is applied that significantly improving prediction performance. The proposed methodology achieved an impressive 95.57% accuracy, outperforming conventional models such as SVM, LR, RF, KNN, XGB. Overall, the PSO-optimized stacked ensemble approach outperforms traditional machine learning techniques in stroke prediction, providing a more accurate and robust model for early detection and intervention.

metadata_raw.tldr: The PSO-optimized stacked ensemble approach outperforms traditional machine learning techniques in stroke prediction, providing a more accurate and robust model for early detection and intervention.

title: Stroke Risk Prediction using Winsorizing Interquartile Range and Tree-Based Classification with Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: According to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study, stroke is the third leading cause of death globally. Recognizing its signs early is crucial for both prevention and effective treatment. Although machine learning has made significant progress in predicting strokes, many current models operate like "black boxes", making them hard to interpret and often resulting in high error rates. This study aims to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability in stroke risk detection by integrating Winsorizing Interquartile Range (IQR) for outlier management, a tree-based classification method, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques. The proposed approach applies Winsorizing Interquartile Range to handle extreme values while employing tree-based methods for prediction due to their superior performance in processing tabular data. Additionally, Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques are utilized to improve model transparency and interpretability. Testing was conducted using the Cerebral Stroke Prediction-Imbalanced Dataset, comparing results with various existing models. The suggested approach demonstrated the lowest prediction error rates, achieving a False Positive Rate (FPR) of 15.74% and a False Negative Rate (FNR) of 8.56%. Additionally, it attained an accuracy of 84.39%, sensitivity of 91.43%, specificity of 84.26%, Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) of 94.74%, and G-Mean of 87.76%, outperforming previous studies in stroke risk prediction. The combination of Winsorizing Interquartile Range, Random Under-Sampling, tree-based classification, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques effectively enhances prediction accuracy and transparency, supporting early stroke detection with improved interpretability. This study contributes to medical informatics by integrating transparent predictive models suitable for decision support systems.

metadata_raw.tldr: The combination of Winsorizing Interquartile Range, Random Under-Sampling, tree-based classification, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques effectively enhances prediction accuracy and transparency, supporting early stroke detection with improved interpretability.

title: Boosting Accuracy in Heart Stroke Risk Prediction through Data Augmentation and ML Optimization
journal: 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Heart stroke is one of the main causes of disease and mortality worldwide. It poses serious global health concerns. Recent epidemiological reports indicate that stroke remains among the primary contributors to disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) worldwide, with millions of individuals affected each year. Since prompt medical intervention can significantly reduce the risk of death and long-term complications, early prediction and prevention are crucial. The research aims to develop a machine learning framework that can accurately and precisely forecast the risk of a heart attack. There are 2,49 stroke cases and 4,861 non-stroke cases in the 5,110 patient records in the dataset, yielding an approximate imbalance ratio of 1:19. Preprocessing included one-hot encoding categorical variables, filling in missing values, and eliminating irrelevant attributes. The Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was employed to address data imbalance, and additional augmentation was applied to increase robustness. A number of algorithms, such as XGBoost (XGB), Random Forest (RF), LightGBM, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression, were tested. With an accuracy of 97.90%, precision of 96.75%, recall of 99.11%, F1-score of 97.92%, and an AUC of 99.79%, XGB demonstrated the best predictive performance among these. These findings demonstrate the potential of ensemble-based gradient boosting methods for stroke prediction in clinical decision support systems. The results show that machine learning models like XGB can be dependable healthcare tools if preprocessing and class imbalance management are done correctly. They have the potential to save many lives by facilitating early diagnosis.

title: Comparative Analysis of Stroke Prediction Models Using Machine Learning
abstract: Stroke remains one of the most critical global health challenges, ranking as the second leading cause of death and the third leading cause of disability worldwide. This study explores the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in predicting stroke risk using demographic, clinical, and lifestyle data from the Stroke Prediction Dataset. By addressing key methodological challenges such as class imbalance and missing data, we evaluated the performance of multiple models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. Our results demonstrate that while these models achieve high accuracy, sensitivity remains a limiting factor for real-world clinical applications.
